# TRACE Environment Setup

This file describes a clean environment setup for running TRACE training, diagnosis evaluation, report-control training, report generation, and PTB-XL report metrics. The tested local environment used Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.5.1, CUDA 11.8, and the Hugging Face/PEFT training stack listed below.

## 1. Create a fresh conda environment

```bash
conda create -n trace python=3.10 -y
conda activate trace
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
```

## 2. Install PyTorch

The tested setup uses PyTorch 2.5.1 with CUDA 11.8. Install the wheel that matches your local CUDA driver and package mirror:

```bash
python -m pip install torch==2.5.1 torchvision torchaudio
```

For a different CUDA version or CPU-only machine, replace this command with the official PyTorch installation command for your system.

## 3. Install TRACE dependencies

```bash
python -m pip install \
  transformers==4.53.0 \
  datasets==3.6.0 \
  peft==0.15.2 \
  trl==0.19.0 \
  accelerate==1.8.1 \
  safetensors==0.5.3 \
  tokenizers==0.21.2 \
  sentencepiece==0.2.1 \
  numpy==1.26.4 \
  pandas==1.4.2 \
  scipy==1.15.3 \
  scikit-learn==1.1.1 \
  wfdb==4.1.2 \
  einops==0.8.1 \
  x-transformers==1.42.11 \
  tensorboard==2.19.0 \
  matplotlib==3.10.0 \
  tqdm==4.67.1 \
  PyYAML==6.0.2 \
  bert-score==0.3.12 \
  pycocoevalcap==1.2
```

`bert-score` is needed only when PTB-XL report metrics are evaluated with `--bertscore`. `pycocoevalcap` is optional because the TRACE metric script defaults to its local metric backend, but it is useful for reproducing COCO-style caption metrics.

## 4. Prepare model and data assets

From the repository root, keep checkpoints under `ckpt/`:

```text
ckpt/
  pretrained_weight/
  ptbxl/
  cpsc2018/
  ningbo/
```

This open-source release keeps only `ckpt/pretrained_weight/CoRe-ECG_mimic_encoder.pth`; dataset-specific weights are generated by the training scripts.

Public dataset files are not redistributed in this repository. Download the public datasets from their original providers and either place the expected metadata files under `data/` or pass explicit paths to the scripts. For PTB-XL, the scripts expect `ptbxl_database.csv` and `scp_statements.csv` unless `--metadata-csv` and `--scp-statements-csv` are provided.

For report generation, make sure the base language model used by the report scripts is available locally or in the Hugging Face cache. If the target machine is offline, pre-download the model and point the scripts to the local model directory.

## 5. Verify the environment

Run these commands from the repository root:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import transformers
import peft
import trl
import wfdb
import x_transformers
print("torch:", torch.__version__)
print("cuda available:", torch.cuda.is_available())
print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
print("peft:", peft.__version__)
print("trl:", trl.__version__)
print("wfdb:", wfdb.__version__)
PY
```

Then check that the main entry points can be parsed or compiled:

```bash
python train_diagnosis_ckpt.py --help
python eval_diagnosis_ptbxl.py --help
python infer_report_ptbxl.py --help
python eval_ptb_report_generation_metrics.py --help
python -m py_compile train_report_ptbxl.py train_report_cpsc2018.py train_report_ningbo.py
```

If these commands complete, the environment is ready for TRACE experiments.
